summary: The type-erasure target is small, minimal, and well-factored: clean public/private discipline (make_any/AnyType/Any public; _make_any/_Content/_any_deleted_ctor private), no dead code, consistent naming, and correct reuse of the canonical _cast/_deref_payload helpers from utils/lowlevel.py rather than reinventing pointer/refcount idioms. The only design observation is a trivial two-line duplication of the payload-wrap idiom between ol_reset and ol_make_any.

findings.title: Payload-wrap idiom duplicated between ol_reset and ol_make_any
findings.claim: The body that erases a value into the Any payload -- wrap in _Content, cast to ErasedType, and record the type code string -- is written twice. In ol_reset (lines 63-66): `self.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType); self.t = ty_code`. In ol_make_any (lines 77-82): `any.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType); any.t = ty_code`. If the erasure contract ever changes (e.g. the _Content wrapping, the cast target type, or the type-code derivation), both sites must be edited in lockstep; missing one silently produces an Any whose stored payload and `.t` tag disagree, which ol_get_as would then either reject or misdecode. This is a maintenance hazard, not a current bug.
findings.evidence: ol_reset closure: `self.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType)` / `self.t = ty_code` (any_type.py:64-65). ol_make_any closure: `any.p = _cast(_Content(x), ErasedType)` / `any.t = ty_code` (any_type.py:79-80). Both derive `ty_code = str(x_ty)` (lines 61, 75). The only difference is the target struct (`self` reset in place vs `new(AnyType)` freshly allocated). _cast and _Content are the canonical helpers (utils/lowlevel.py:28, content_wrap.py:17), so the duplicated logic is the two assignment lines, not the primitives.
findings.recommendation: Optional, low priority. Either have ol_make_any's closure delegate to the same in-place population that ol_reset uses (call `_.reset(x)` style on the freshly `new`-ed struct), or factor the two-line set into a single overloaded `_set_any_payload(target, x, ty_code)` helper used by both. Given the duplication is only two lines and both sites are in one file, leaving it as-is is also defensible; the change is local and low risk but the benefit is marginal.
